episodes.199870: A squall line developed ahead of a cold front leading to wind damage in southeast NC.
episodes.200113: A cold front pushed through the region within an environment displaying high shear and modest instability, producing thunderstorms capable of damaging wind gusts across coastal waters.
episodes.200175: A cold front extending northeast to southwest across central North Carolina slowly pushed eastwards through the afternoon and evening eventually pushing offshore during the overnight hours of the seventh and into the eighth. Along and out ahead of this front, a line of rain and thunderstorm activity was ongoing across western NC and the Triad during the morning of April seventh. This activity then tracked east through the afternoon and evening impacting all coastal waters. Strong wind gusts were the primary hazard within the strongest storms.
episodes.200233: A line of showers and thunderstorms followed a warm front across the Middle Ohio Valley and Central Appalachians during the morning of April 3rd. A cold front brought more precipitation into the area the night of the 3rd and then stalled over West Virginia through the morning of the 4th. Showers continued in the vicinity of the boundary, which slid to the south the afternoon of the 4th before being lifted north as a warm front again on the 5th. Another cold front arrived the evening of the 5th and once again stalled over West Virginia. Precipitation eventually tapered off as the front sank to the southeast on the 7th.||A total of three to five inches of rain fell in southeast Ohio. Numerous roads were closed due to flooding and water began to approach some homes as creeks and streams rose out of their banks. Water rescues were eventually needed as vehicles became stranded in flood waters. Portions of Symmes Creek, Raccoon Creek, Duck Creek, Shade River, Little Muskingum River, Muskingum River, and the Hocking River all experienced flooding.
episodes.200699: Pre-front thunderstorms moved across an unstable airmass during the afternoon and evening as a strong 500 mb 55-70 kt jet moved across the area providing additional dynamical support and enhanced unidirectional shear.
episodes.200700: Pre-front thunderstorms moved across an unstable airmass during the afternoon and evening as a strong 500 mb 55-70 kt jet moved across the area providing additional dynamical support and enhanced unidirectional shear.
episodes.200826: A frontal boundary passed through South Florida on April 8th bringing scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. With passing thunderstorms in the morning, winds became gusty across the local Atlantic waters.
episodes.201527: A cold front swept through the southern Appalachian region on April 6th, producing several hours of moderate to heavy rainfall in the mountains of east Tennessee and western North Carolina. Runoff from this event resulted in the Pigeon River at Newport going into minor flood stage from late in the evening on April 7th and lasting into the early morning hours on April 8th.
episodes.202105: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along a stationary front and area of low pressure April 7 and 8. This activity brought gusty winds to the Chesapeake Bay, Rivers, Atlantic Coastal Waters, and Currituck Sound from the afternoon hours April 7 into the early morning hours of April 8.
episodes.202264: Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred offshore Key Largo, Florida, in association with a thunderstorm moving eastward along a pre-frontal trough moving through the Florida Keys.
episodes.203945: Heavy rainfall over a multiday period brought flooding to many rivers across Arkansas. Points along the White, Black, Cache, and Ouachita Rivers remained in flood through the remainder of the month.
